agent_index.rule: one compact JSON line on stdout, derived from this manifest only; run it first, then read the route in docs/agent/index.yaml

behavior_changes.change: every absolute /home/lmbullo/loop literal is gone; ROOT derives from __file__, overridable via LOOP_ROOT (sandbox) and LOOP_RUNS (artifacts)

loop.py -> harness/agent.py + harness/api.py + harness/tools.py, reached as 'run.py api'; sim.py/drive.py -> harness/sim1.py + scenarios/*.json; sim2.py/drive2.py -> harness/sim2.py + scenarios/*.json
fixtures/ replaced ws1 and ws2; each sim run mounts a fresh copy, so sims are repeatable and drive2's hardcoded reset is deleted
fixtures/ws1/src/analyze.py is the buggy baseline copied from drive2.py's reset literal, not the leftover repaired file
root obs/ and obs2/ moved under the run dir; api observation files are numbered per observation (obs-<k>) instead of per turn, so batched calls no longer overwrite each other
api refuses to start without credentials (exit 3) and reports api errors as exit 4 instead of exit 0
sim transcripts are written to .logs/<sim>/<label>/log.json as json arrays (the old files were named .jsonl but held arrays); sim2 now persists its log too
exec failures report 'TypeName: message' on both wires; sim1 previously returned str(e) alone
a relative cwd in a transcript step resolves against the run workspace, not the invoker's cwd
header text names obs/ under the run dir instead of .obs/<id>; token counts differ by a few bytes from records/sim1-*.json
sim1/sim2 print a final 'summary: {json}' line for machine consumption; api writes .logs/api/summary.json
runs/ -> .logs/: config.runs() defaults to <ROOT>/.logs; runs, usage, log.json, summary, observations, server.log, registry, pidfile and socket all live there

api is no longer one process per task: 'run.py api' auto-attaches to the tree's daemon over .logs/server.sock (spawning it when absent) and streams turn/tool/obs/done/cost events; the daemon owns the run, so a killed client does not stop it

harness/agent.py loop semantics are unchanged (append-only messages, reasoning stripped before re-send, bounded ingest, meter-not-gate, four tools); prints became events the daemon emits and the client renders
api gains exit 5 (server unavailable); 3 and 4 now arrive as an error event from the daemon and are returned by the client
summary.json gains exit and run_id; usage.jsonl, log.json and obs/ are still written by the run itself, now inside the daemon

the daemon owns no run: it appends to .logs/runs/<run_id>/record.jsonl and keeps only caches (current run id, subscribers, writer). kill -9 leaves completed records byte-identical and marks nothing complete that is not
.logs/api/{log.json,usage.jsonl,summary.json} replaced by one append-only record per run; an event is one O_APPEND write + fsync, so a crash loses at most the in-flight turn
daemon start (and stop) scans .logs/runs for records without a terminal end and appends interrupted to each unlocked one; a record held by a live executor is left alone
new 'run.py view [RUN_ID]': pure formatter over record bytes, --json canonical document, '-' reads it back, --list and --schema; works with the daemon stopped and from any cwd
new 'run.py resume RUN_ID': rebuilds the message list from the record, appends resume+turn*+end; refuses complete, corrupt, or live-locked records
per-run artifacts moved from .logs/api/* to .logs/runs/<run_id>/{record.jsonl,record.lock,obs/}; saved observation paths in the wire are run-relative

daemon -> client lines are the record events themselves (run_start, turn, resume, error, interrupted, end) after one hello line; the client renders them with the same function view uses, so live output and 'view' agree
run ids are UTC-sortable (<stamp>Z-<8 hex>); 'most recent run' is max(run_id), not an in-memory cursor
api runs the loop in the client process and writes the record itself; the daemon no longer executes runs, so stopping or restarting it cannot interrupt one
assistant text is dropped before it is stored or re-sent; a turn with no tool call ends the run with finish=no_tool_call
busy names the holder pid and says one run per tree; write reports replaced=/appended_to=; the header states the tree lock, one run per tree, and literal argv
the daemon owns waiting tasks in .logs/queue.json; TUIs enqueue/drop/move through the socket and render the same snapshot
each run executes in a detached worker process with its own session; the control plane can be killed or restarted without interrupting it
a new daemon scans .logs/workers/ and .logs/queue.json for live workers and reports the in-flight run
server reload bumps .logs/reload.json; workers re-import api/config/observe/tools/pricing and refresh the system header at the next turn boundary
server restart replaces the daemon only; live workers survive and finish, and the replacement daemon reattaches from disk
stop and restart refuse while a worker run is live unless --force, which first names the run, worker pid and task
tui/ is a polling renderer over the daemon snapshot; it holds no queue or run authority and is not imported by any server module
the loop derives its message list from the record by folding events; resume and start are the same code path, and recrebuild.py is gone

tui rows are fitted to their cell width and truncated with an ellipsis, the current task is one row carrying id, state, turns, cost, finish, detail and task text in that order, prompt rows use the full terminal width and reflow to one line when it fits, wrapped rows do not start with a break-created gap, and status/position indicators keep an exact width

tui colors are a grey base with gruvbox accents: 256-color approximations when the terminal has them, an eight-color fallback otherwise; every pair keeps the terminal default background (-1), and tui/theme.py init_colors is the only initializer

the tui is plain text: no color pairs, bold or reverse video; selection is a leading '>' marker. Plain text always opens the prompt, so j/k/K/J/x/d navigation is gone. Arrows select and toggle the task/queue pane, shift+up/down reorder the queue, delete drops, enter types, ctrl+q quits

tui colors come from tui/theme.py: a neutral grey chrome scale plus muted state hues (accent, ok, warn, err), every pair on the terminal default background (-1). The prompt box is grey in both focus states (muted when idle, strong when focused); no role is green on the prompt, and there is no bold, reverse video or per-line color noise
the prompt box draws a horizontal rule as its top and bottom edge, so both edges stay visible; the prompt label sits in the top rule and at least one row separates the two rules

tui rows use state glyphs (● running, ✓ complete, ■ interrupted, ✕ error, ○ idle/queued), a › selection marker, short run ids, middle-dot metadata separators and ↵/↑↓/⇧↑↓/←→ key hints; metadata is muted, task text stays strong, and section headers carry counts

the tui body is split into running, queued and done sections in that order: queued is omitted when the queue is empty and keeps its newest items at the bottom when it overflows; done lists terminal runs newest first from the daemon snapshot, capped and fitted to one line, and the current run never appears there

the tui derives its done history from record bytes when the daemon is down or its snapshot predates the done field, skipping runs still held by a live worker, so finished tasks survive a fire-and-forget worker and are visible without restarting the control plane

with focus on the task area, up/down/page/home/end move one selection across the running row and the done list; the done section scrolls to keep the selected run visible, marks it with the selection chevron, and its header shows the visible range whenever it is scrolled; leaving task focus keeps the done scroll, and the running row is marked only when the selection is on it

enter on the selected task row opens a full-body log view built from record bytes: one fitted, ellipsised line per tool call (turn, name, compact args, observation) plus one final row for the result, interruption, error or pending summary; the visible window is exactly the terminal height, so it grows and shrinks with the terminal without padding, and esc/enter returns to the task list

task focus carries one flat arrow-key selection over the running row, every queued item and every done run in display order; both CSI arrows and SS3 application-cursor arrows are accepted, queued rows are marked and scrolled into view without switching panes, the queue cursor follows the flat selection, left/right keeps the selected queue item, enter opens a run log for running/done rows and leaves a queued row selected with a notice, and the status hint reads ↑↓ tasks

the log view scrolls independently of its selection: mouse wheel or shift+up/down moves the viewport without moving the marked call, the range header follows it, and the next arrow/page/home/end re-anchors the selection; wheel tracking is enabled while the TUI runs

the prompt box opens from every focus with tab/backtab or the first typed character; opening it from a run log keeps the log visible above the prompt, and esc/tab returns to that log (or the queue) with the draft preserved, while submit still returns to the task list

the loop's terminal turn stores its text as the run result instead of discarding it (no_tool_call only when the turn is empty); recread.live_state marks a run with a live worker running instead of interrupted, so listings stop calling live runs interrupted; write accepts content as an alias for data and exec/write/edit return bad_args instead of KeyError; tui/probe.py renders a snapshot headlessly

ctrl+x cancels the task row carrying the selection chevron: a queued row is dropped from the daemon queue, a live run is signalled through the socket and records an interruption, and a finished run is refused with a notice; the cancel request is the daemon 'cancel' command and the task/queue status hints name ^X

the log view shows the run's full final summary instead of a 240-character one-line excerpt: runlog keeps its paragraphs, the summary head (check glyph, 'result', dash) is followed by every wrapped continuation row, scroll is measured in display rows so a long summary can be read a screen at a time, and a newly selected summary anchors at its first row instead of being clipped

docs/agent/* are YAML (schema loop-agent-doc/1) instead of Markdown; the old README+index are merged into docs/agent/index.yaml; root AGENTS.md and README.md stay Markdown entry points; records the current contract: a second api queues a front item instead of attaching, a terminal no-tool reply ends done with its text as result, listings show running for a live interrupted record, write accepts a content alias

a task may carry a verify command; the worker declares it in a verify event before the first turn and runs it after the terminal turn, appending exit/note (view derives ok) before end. no verify means no event, which view shows as absent rather than an assumed pass. agent.py is now the loop only; fold.py holds the pure event-to-request functions

config.runs() defaults to root()/.logs and registry.tree() keys on root(), so LOOP_ROOT alone makes a directory a complete workspace: its own daemon, socket, queue and runs. Unset LOOP_ROOT keeps the previous behaviour (the directory containing run.py)

run.py --json prints one compact loop-index/1 line derived from manifest.json (entrypoints, checks, scenarios, docs, invariants, env, layout, record, wire) so an agent bootstraps in one command without walking the tree; the index carries no absolute paths
README.md and AGENTS.md are machine-first: bootstrap via run.py --json, exact command and route tables, normative invariants, no human-facing prose or duplicated narrative

an observation saved for bounding now reports a root-relative path (.logs/runs/<run_id>/obs/obs-<k>.txt) instead of a run-relative one, so the agent can read it from the run cwd without knowing the run id; an obs dir outside the run root reports an absolute path; a tool name that is not exec/write/edit/done returns err unknown_tool instead of a bogus edit bad_args; an edit match failure names the path

drag-copy: a left-button drag on any view reverse-highlights screen cells, and release copies the covered text (one line per row) through OSC 52 plus the first installed wl-copy/xclip/xsel/pbcopy helper, then clears the highlight; shift-drag and non-left buttons are left to the terminal

the task queue/done sections and the log view share a one-cell right-edge scroll indicator: a muted track and strong thumb computed from the existing window total/visible/scroll state, no bar when every row fits, and one content cell reserved while it is visible so text is never covered; it recomputes on resize and content changes and stays consistent across both views

the task view scrolls independently of its selection: mouse wheel or shift+arrows move the done viewport, or the queued viewport when the selection sits in the queue, without moving the selection chevron; the running/queued/done layout and its shared right-edge indicator stay, offsets clamp to the body above the prompt, and resize or content changes recompute the window; any arrow/page/home/end re-anchors the selected row

the system header is constant across runs: max_inline, task and root are no longer interpolated into the prefix, and done/parallel-call guidance replaces the false claim that every no-call turn is no_tool_call; run_start.max_inline now pins only the observation bound, whose default drops from 32768 to 8192 bytes so a large dump is saved and summarized instead of re-sent as a hit on every later turn; the summary now warns that a whole re-read would be summarized again, so the agent greps or reads a small range instead of paging the entire file

a terminal turn with no tool call and no text is not final on its own: after turn 1 one nudge user message is recorded as a nudge event and folded into the next request, then an empty stop ends as no_tool_call; a non-str done.result becomes an error observation instead of a record-validation crash; per-turn response parsing, tool dispatch and the stop policy move to harness/turn.py so agent.py stays under the 200-line limit
sim1 and sim2 no longer hard-code cache rates; their projections call pricing.cost, the same manifest-backed owner as the live loop

exec rejects standalone shell operators and shell-keyword argv[0] with err shell_syntax naming the sh -c form instead of spawning a command that cannot work; the system header tells the model to script a repeated probe instead of repeating single-step calls

invariants.rule: no knowledge of repos, tests or languages
verbatim, modified only by the bounding rule; text over run_start.max_inline is saved and summarized
a terminal turn with no tool call and no text is not final after turn 1: one nudge user message is recorded and retried; a second silent stop ends with finish=no_tool_call
api.header() is constant across runs; task and run-specific values enter after it, and run_start.max_inline pins only the observation bound
a verify event is evidence, not a gate: the command is declared before the first turn, its exit is stored after the terminal turn, and view derives ok=1/0; no command means no event and never a pass
never mutated in place; each sim run copies its fixture into .logs/<sim>/<label>/ws/
no absolute paths in code or config; roots come from __file__ or env; frozen records/ artifacts may carry historical /home/... strings as data, never as inputs
run.py is the only entry point; modules are import-only (the daemon is spawned as 'run.py server _daemon')
one append-only record per run under .logs/runs/<run_id>/; each event is one fsynced line; end is the only completion marker; a kill -9 loses at most the in-flight turn
nothing a run produced exists only in a process: record bytes are enough to read, render and resume it; queue and worker state are also files under .logs/
view is a pure function of record bytes: no server, no network, no clock, no cwd; --json round-trips into the text form
the daemon owns queue and worker state but executes no run; killing or restarting it cannot interrupt a worker
a TUI reads a daemon snapshot and sends requests; it never owns a run or holds authoritative state, and server code never imports tui/

purpose.core_question: Can coding work be done through one exec waist, with bounded, cache-friendly observations?
purpose.summary: Research harness for a tool-calling agent loop; compares tool/observation designs by token cost and correctness. The daemon owns a durable queue and a worker registry; each run executes in a detached worker process. Every run is one durable record; inspection is a pure function over those bytes.

envelope.data: object whose fields are fixed by type in events[type].data
envelope.seq: 1, 2, 3, ... contiguous from the first event; never reused
envelope.ts: UTC ISO-8601 YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ, taken when the event was appended

line.format: one JSON object per line, LF terminated, no embedded newline
line.partial_tail: a final line without LF is a torn write: dropped on the next append; complete events are never modified
line.write: one O_APPEND write of one line, then fsync, before the next turn begins

record.path_note: one record per run, co-located with its obs/: .logs/runs/<run_id>/{record.jsonl,record.lock,obs/}; the tree-wide executor lock is .logs/run.lock
record.rebuild: msgs = [system(api.header()), user(run_start.task)] + per turn: [turn.message] + [tool(call.id, call.observation) for call in turn.calls], plus [nudge.text as a user message] at its seq; the system header is constant across runs and run_start.max_inline pins only the observation bound

run_id.order: lexicographic order equals chronological order; newest run = max

state.empty: no events at all; resume appends a resume event and rebuilds the run without run_start
state.interrupted: any last event other than end: a kill -9 leaves no process to write a marker, so the missing end is the marker
state.marker: an interrupted event records who noticed and why (server_start, server_stop, worker_lost); it is never required for the state
state.listing: state=running when state=interrupted and a live worker registry entry holds the run; the record state itself stays interrupted

view.derived_tail: when state != complete and the last event is not interrupted: one '[interrupted] reason=no_terminal_event' line; when torn_tail_bytes > 0: one '[torn]' line
view.round_trip: python3 run.py view --json RUN | python3 run.py view -
view.text: one line group per event in seq order; newlines and tabs are escaped, carriage returns are dropped

server.address_long_path: falls back to $TMPDIR/loop-<sha256(.logs)[:16]>.sock when the path exceeds 100 bytes; the address is always recorded in the registry, never guessed
server.concurrency: one live worker per tree, enforced by the queue and .logs/run.lock; a second 'api' queues a front item and streams it behind the live run; 'resume' while a run is in flight is refused (exit 5)
server.idempotency: start = probe -> clean stale -> spawn -> wait ready, all under .logs/server.lock; N invocations yield one process
server.ownership: the daemon owns waiting tasks in .logs/queue.json and the on-disk worker registry in .logs/workers/; a run is the record at .logs/runs/<run_id>/record.jsonl plus the detached worker that holds its lock. Clients only connect, read records and send requests.
server.process: one control-plane daemon per code tree; spawned detached by 'server start'; it owns the queue and worker registry but never executes a model turn

protocol.out: one hello line then record events from disk, ending at type=end or interrupted; snapshot replies are the shared queue/current/last/cost view

queue.advance: the supervisor promotes one waiting item when no worker is live and spawns a detached worker

reconcile.never: silently adopted, silently dropped, or deleted
reconcile.rule: a record whose last event is not end and whose executor lock is free gets one interrupted event appended; a locked record with a live worker is left alone; a corrupt record is never rewritten
reconcile.when: daemon start and every supervisor tick while the current worker is not live

reload.never: no process restart and no interruption of the in-flight turn
reapplies: constant system header; run_start.max_inline pins observations
reload.when: each worker checks the generation at its next turn boundary; the next fold picks up edited module text

restart.action: replace the control-plane process; detached workers are left running
restart.guard: refuse while a worker run is live unless --force; --force names the run and worker pid it detaches
restart.reattach: the new daemon reads .logs/queue.json and .logs/workers/ and reports the live run

server.stale_state: dead pid, dead socket, corrupt registry entry are cleaned and replaced by the next start; no user resolution required

stateless.attach: a client attaching to a run is served the record from disk as backlog, then live events
stateless.fresh_daemon: answers for every run and every queued item from .logs alone; status and runs scan records, queue and worker state, never daemon memory
stateless.kill_9: workers survive; a replacement daemon reattaches from .logs/queue.json and .logs/workers/
stateless.memory: caches only: the accepted socket and the spawned child handles used for reaping

stop.effect: stop the control plane; without a live run it is a no-op
stop.guard: refuse while a worker run is live unless --force; --force names the run, worker pid and task it interrupts

worker.lifetime: independent of the daemon and of every client; 'server restart' leaves it running
worker.lost: a dead worker with no live lock is reconciled to interrupted by the daemon supervisor
worker.process: one detached process per run: 'run.py server _worker <run_id>'
worker.reattach: a new daemon scans .logs/workers/ and treats a live pid + matching proc_start as the current run
worker.state: .logs/workers/<run_id>.json (run_id, pid, proc_start, state, item_id, task, root, started_at, started_ts, seq, turns, cost, exit)

mobile.transport: HTTP/1.1 JSON over one private or loopback address; bearer token on every /v1 route; cleartext on local Wi-Fi only
mobile.bind: host must be a literal private/loopback IP; 0.0.0.0, multicast and public addresses are refused
mobile.auth: Authorization: Bearer <LOOP_MOBILE_TOKEN or .logs/mobile.token>; constant-time compare; non-private peers get 403
mobile.lifecycle: server mobile start|status|stop; the listener lives in the daemon, so daemon stop/restart closes it and workers are unaffected
mobile.roots: LOOP_MOBILE_ROOTS or repeated --root; every selected path is realpath-contained in an allowlisted root; hidden dirs and escaping symlinks are omitted
mobile.limits: task <= 20000 chars; body <= 64 KiB; directory listing <= 500 children
mobile.authority: the bridge calls the existing queue, snapshot and record projection functions; it has no queue, run or state of its own

api.obs_name: obs-<k>.txt, k counts observations over the whole run
api.saved_paths: root-relative (.logs/runs/<run_id>/obs/obs-<k>.txt) so the agent reads it from the run cwd; absolute when obs/ sits outside the run root
api.shape: <binary> 'kind=binary bytes= sha256= head_hex=' | <inline> raw text | <big> 'kind=text bytes= lines= saved=' + a note against a whole re-read + first15 + last5; a line appears once, and last5 is omitted when all lines fit in first15
api.sink: .logs/runs/<run_id>/record.jsonl; one event per line, fsynced before the next turn

sim1.bounding: payload <= 1000B inline, else head 600B + tail 400B + saved file

sim2.bounding: ANSI stripped; empty -> ''; binary -> sha256+head_hex; >2000B -> 'kind=text lines= first= last= saved=' ; else inline with blank-run collapse

stop.done: non-empty terminal text -> finish=done with result=text.strip()
stop.nudge: empty terminal text on turn > 1 with no earlier nudge -> one nudge user message, then another turn
stop.no_tool_call: empty terminal text on turn 1 or after one nudge -> finish=no_tool_call
stop.tools: a turn with tool_calls always continues; done in the call list settles without dispatch

verify.absent: no command -> no verify event; never a pass
verify.evidence: first non-blank line of stdout+stderr cut to 180 chars plus ' ms=<duration>'; no output -> 'no output ms=<duration>'
verify.order: declare {command,ran:false,exit:null,note:null} before the first turn; run after the terminal turn; append {ran:true,exit,note} before end
verify.shell: sh -c CMD, 120000 ms timeout, process-group kill
verify.status: the event stores exit; view renders ok=1 when exit==0 and ok=0 otherwise; status never gates the run

view.text: compact, one line group per event
